_: WHERE EVERY ANDROID SIGNING FINGERPRINT COMES FROM. This file is NEVER
deployed: it lives beside site/, not inside it. assetlinks.json is parsed
by Android and holds nothing but canonical Digital Asset Links; the notes
that make it governable are here, and tests/doctrine-app-links.js is what
ties the two together.
A fingerprint may appear in assetlinks.json only if it appears here with
status `vouched`. `awaited` is a slot declared before its key exists.
`unattributed` is a value nobody can trace, and it is refused from
assetlinks.json by name.
kind: debug | release | store. A debug key and a publication key may not
be SERVED from assetlinks.json at the same time -- the gate enforces
that, so the question is put on the day it becomes real rather than the
day someone remembers.
THAT RULE USED TO READ THIS FILE INSTEAD OF THE DEPLOYMENT, AND ON 17
AUGUST 2026 IT DEADLOCKED. Vouching the publication key below -- an act
of pure record-keeping, changing nothing any device can reach -- fired
tests/doctrine-app-links.js, while scripts/check-apk-signing.sh refuses
any state in which debug-local is NOT vouched, because the debug lane of
apk.yml holds the certificate it reads off its artefact against that
entry. No state of this file satisfied both; all three were applied to a
copy that day and all three failed.
Neither gate was weakened. The rule was asking the wrong question: the
harm its own comment named was a debug key in a production
assetlinks.json, and the condition it evaluated was a debug key in this
ledger. `vouched` here means somebody wrote down which key a value comes
from and how to recompute it -- a PRECONDITION of serving, as the
paragraph above says, and not the act of it. Since 17 August 2026 the
rule reads what assetlinks.json serves, and it fires on the day the
publication fingerprint is served alongside the debug one, which is what
publishing to any device that carries nothing yet requires.
THE DECISION IS STILL UNMADE, and it is now attached to the day it
matters instead of to this file's redness: see debug-local's
withdraw_when, and .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-17-publication/
task-M-report.md for what each way out costs.

fingerprints.name: debug-local
fingerprints.origin: The debug keystore committed at packages/app/android/app/debug.keystore, which is what `signingConfigs.debug` names and therefore what every device build of this repository is signed with. It was a per-machine ~/.android/debug.keystore until 2026-09-06, which was wrong twice over: the value differed on every developer's laptop, and it was not the key the application actually carried -- installing a build over another failed with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, which is how it was found.
fingerprints.reproduce: keytool -list -v -keystore packages/app/android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android -alias androiddebugkey | grep SHA256:
fingerprints.withdraw_when: WITHDRAWN FROM SERVICE ON 7 SEPTEMBER 2026, BY THE ACCOUNT HOLDER, AND STILL VOUCHED. The entry above described the condition as the field rather than the keyring, and the field moved: #91's trial installs from the internal testing track, and a build from that track had no App Links verification at all while this key was the one served. WHAT IT COST, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: https://messagr.eu/i/<token> no longer opens the application on the two phones carrying an install signed by this key -- the demonstration Pixel that AGENTS.md 7.2 freezes, and the APK the maintainer handed his friend. This entry said until 13 September 2026 that both kept an entry path through the landing page's Copy the link. Neither did: the application has no field to paste a link into and does not read the clipboard, so a phone whose https links open the browser has no way in from the page. Neither is uninstalled and neither loses an account. AND WHAT IT BOUGHT WAS NOT ONLY #114. This keystore is committed at packages/app/android/app/debug.keystore in a PUBLIC repository, so while its fingerprint was served anybody could build an application Android would verify as a legitimate handler of messagr.eu invitation links. The ticket describes the opposite symptom; this is the same fix seen from the other side, and it is the sharper half. It stays vouched because scripts/check-apk-signing.sh reads the debug lane's artefact against this entry, and because vouching is record-keeping rather than service.

fingerprints.name: debug-machine
fingerprints.origin: The maintainer's own ~/.android/debug.keystore, which is what signed builds installed by hand before 6 September 2026. IT IS BACK BECAUSE OF A PHONE NOBODY CAN ASK. This registry named it alone until today, when the served value was corrected to the keystore committed in this repository -- the one every build here is actually signed with, measured off the Pixel. But the APK the maintainer handed his friend predates that correction and may carry either. Serving one and not the other would leave that phone's invitation links opening a browser, and there is no way to find out which it holds without asking somebody to check. Both are debug keys, so the rule that refuses a debug key beside a publication key is untouched: this widens nothing.
fingerprints.reproduce: keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -storepass android | grep SHA256: -- on the maintainer's machine and nowhere else, which is half of why it stopped being the value this file served.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: WITHDRAWN FROM SERVICE ON 7 SEPTEMBER 2026, with debug-local and for the same reason: a publication fingerprint is now served, and a debug key may not be served beside one. It goes on being unreproducible outside the maintainer's machine, which is why it was always to go first; it simply went at the same moment instead. This entry said until 13 September 2026 that the friend's phone kept an entry path through Copy the link, as the Pixel did. Neither did: the application has no field to paste a link into.

fingerprints.name: release
fingerprints.origin: The maintainer's publication keystore, the one ~/.messagr-signature/identifiants.env names in MAGASIN: self-signed CN=Messagr, O=Messagr, C=FR, a 4096-bit RSA key signed SHA384withRSA, created 8 August 2026 and valid until 24 December 2053. It is the key a release is signed with -- `releaseKeystorePath` in android/app/build.gradle.kts and the three settings beside it name it from outside the repository, and `requireReleaseSigningMaterial` refuses to package a release without all four. THIS IS THE VALUE messagr.eu SERVED FROM 9 AUGUST 2026, and it sat in this registry as `unattributed-2026-08-09` for eight days for one reason: the task that wrote the registry searched its own worktree, found nothing but ~/.android/debug.keystore, and concluded that nothing here reproduced the value. The keystore was two directories outside that worktree and nobody looked there. The dates agree with the attribution -- the keystore is of 8 August 2026 and commit 385d26b imported the value on 9 August. Measured on 17 August 2026 with the command below and compared character for character against what site/.well-known/assetlinks.json served until 16 August 2026.
fingerprints.reproduce: . ~/.messagr-signature/identifiants.env && keytool -list -v -keystore "$MAGASIN" -alias "$ALIAS" -storepass "$MOT_DE_PASSE" | grep 'SHA256'  --  that file holds the keystore path, the alias and the password, and it is named here BY PATH AND NEVER BY CONTENT. A path is not a secret and is useful only to somebody already on this machine; refusing to name it would protect nothing and would cost the reproducibility this registry exists for.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: Never, as long as the application is published. This is the identity a store checks the upload against, and a copy already installed will not accept an update signed by anything else. If Play App Signing is turned on it stops being the certificate that reaches devices -- the three play-app-signing entries below are then the ones that do -- but it stays the upload key and it stays here.

fingerprints.name: play-app-signing
fingerprints.origin: The classic certificate Google Play generates when Play App Signing re-signs the upload: the upload key signs what is sent to Google, and Google signs what is sent to a phone. Read off the console by the account holder on 6 September 2026 and pasted verbatim. THIS ENTRY SAID UNTIL 13 SEPTEMBER 2026 THAT IT WAS THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY REACHES DEVICES. It reaches only those at API level 37 (Android 17) and above: apksigner on the base.apk of an install from the closed testing track lists it as 'V3.2 Hybrid Classical Signer (minSdkVersion=37)', the classic half of Play's hybrid signature, matched character for character that day. Every earlier device presents play-app-signing-v3 below, which is why no phone below Android 17 verified messagr.eu links while only this certificate and its post-quantum twin were served.
fingerprints.reproduce: Play Console, the application, Protected by Play, App signing (direct: .../app/<id>/keymanagement): 'App signing key certificate', column 'Classic key', SHA-256. Or on an install from a Play track: adb shell pm path eu.messagr, adb pull the base.apk it names, then apksigner verify --print-certs -v base.apk, line 'V3.2 Hybrid Classical Signer ... certificate SHA-256 digest'.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: The application leaves Google Play. SERVED SINCE 7 SEPTEMBER 2026: the account holder took the choice this file had attached to the day it mattered, and that day was #91's trial installing from the internal testing track. Served with its post-quantum twin and never without it, and from 13 September 2026 beside play-app-signing-v3: the three are one Play signing identity as three generations of Android see it.

fingerprints.name: play-app-signing-pq
fingerprints.origin: The post-quantum certificate Play generates alongside the classic one -- the console shows both, labelled 'Classic key' and 'Post-quantum cryptographic key', and marks the signing key 'ready for quantum computing (beta)'. Read off the console by the account holder on 6 September 2026 and pasted verbatim. It was recorded because which certificate a device presents to Digital Asset Links verification is not something this project decides: it depends on the device and its Android version. THE REASONING HELD AND THE COUNT DID NOT. apksigner on an install from the closed testing track, on 13 September 2026, lists this one as 'V3.2 Hybrid PQC Signer (minSdkVersion=37)', an ML-DSA key honoured from API level 37 only, and lists a third certificate that was not among those read off the console, play-app-signing-v3, the only one a device below API level 37 can present. Declaring fewer than all of them is the defect this file exists to prevent, and from 7 to 13 September 2026 it happened: no phone below Android 17 verified messagr.eu links.
fingerprints.reproduce: Play Console, the application, Protected by Play, App signing (direct: .../app/<id>/keymanagement): 'App signing key certificate', column 'Post-quantum cryptographic key', SHA-256. Or on an install from a Play track: apksigner verify --print-certs -v base.apk, line 'V3.2 Hybrid PQC Signer ... certificate SHA-256 digest'.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: With its classic twin, and never separately: they are two certificates for one signing identity, and serving one without the other is the fleet-splitting defect described above. SERVED SINCE 7 SEPTEMBER 2026, together, and from 13 September 2026 beside play-app-signing-v3.

fingerprints.name: play-app-signing-v3
fingerprints.origin: The certificate Google Play signs the APK Signature Scheme v3.0 block with (CN=Android, OU=Android, O=Google Inc., L=Mountain View, ST=California, C=US, RSA 4096), and therefore THE ONE EVERY DEVICE BELOW API LEVEL 37 PRESENTS, which in September 2026 means every Android release before Android 17. It was not among the certificates read off the console on 6 September 2026. Measured on 13 September 2026 on a Galaxy S22 Ultra on Android 16 holding version 130 from the closed testing track: pm get-app-links eu.messagr named it as the package signature and answered messagr.eu: 1024 while assetlinks.json served only play-app-signing and play-app-signing-pq, and apksigner on the base.apk pulled from that phone reported it as 'V3.0 Signer' beside the two 'V3.2 Hybrid' signers (minSdkVersion=37) that match those two entries.
fingerprints.reproduce: On a device that installed from a Play track: adb shell pm path eu.messagr, adb pull the base.apk it names, then apksigner verify --print-certs -v base.apk, line 'V3.0 Signer: certificate SHA-256 digest'. The device says the same in the Signatures line of adb shell pm get-app-links eu.messagr.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: The application leaves Google Play, or Play stops writing a v3.0 block because the application's minSdkVersion reaches 37, and then only once apksigner on an install from the track lists no V3.0 Signer. SERVED FROM 13 SEPTEMBER 2026, beside play-app-signing and play-app-signing-pq: the three are one Play signing identity as three generations of Android see it, and serving fewer than all of them splits the fleet.
